page: Microsoft Azure FX32-8ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using x86_64 architecture, clocked at 4.2 GHz. It is paired with an exceptionally large memory allocation of 672.0 GB of RAM, equating to 84.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and a notable 260 MB L3 cache pool. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (both tile and int8), and cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero GPUs and no bundled local storage, requiring remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate and instruction support. Geekbench scores show a top-tier single-core score of 2369.0 and top-tier text processing at 2937.0, along with strong single-threaded throughput in gzip compression (34.8 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.36 GB/sec). However, multi-core metrics settle into mid-tier territory due to the 8-vCPU count, as observed in the Geekbench multi-core score (8692.0) and stress-ng multi-core CPU test (8881.34). Memory benchmarks show 691.25 GB/sec cached small-block throughput and 72.43 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth.

Cost efficiency is centered around software-licensing optimization and high memory density. By exposing only 8 vCPUs alongside 672.0 GB of RAM, workloads that require large in-memory capacities but are billed on a per-core license model gain substantial economic advantage. Conversely, workloads that do not leverage the vast RAM pool or that require massive parallel throughput will experience poor benchmark-per-resource efficiency.

The instance is best suited for memory-bound applications that demand fast single-core throughput, such as large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), caching tiers, and memory-intensive enterprise software with per-core licensing constraints. It is poorly suited for large-model LLM generation or high-parallelism tasks without hardware accelerators.
description: Microsoft Azure FX32-8ms_v2 is a specialized compute- and memory-intensive instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside an expansive 672.0 GB of RAM, or 84.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core capabilities, registering 2369.0 on Geekbench single-core, alongside solid decompression and text processing speeds, while multi-core metrics align with its 8-vCPU footprint. The high memory-to-core ratio offers cost efficiency for workloads constrained by per-core software licensing. FX32-8ms_v2 is optimal for memory-bound relational and in-memory databases, EDA tooling, and intensive cache architectures.
